exceptions.diagnosis: Model is underforecasting OEM orders because Samsung reduced orders 3 months ago and the model has not been retrained to reflect the new baseline

alert.title: Model is underforecasting OEM display glass — Samsung order baseline has shifted and the model hasn't caught up
alert.desc: Samsung reduced its display glass orders 3 months ago, establishing a lower order baseline. The forecasting model was last retrained 14 months ago and does not reflect this shift — it continues to forecast against the higher pre-reduction baseline, producing systematic overforecasts. The bias has been worsening for 3 straight cycles. The fix requires a model retrain with refreshed ACV distribution data — a one-off override will not resolve the structural misalignment.

rca.finding: The model is overforecasting OEM display glass because Samsung reduced orders 3 months ago and the model hasn't been retrained to reflect the new baseline. All data feeds are healthy — direct B2B and OEM distributor feeds are current with no pipeline failures. The problem is the ACV (all commodity volume) weighted distribution used to calibrate OEM order expectations: its drift score is 0.81 against a 0.50 threshold, reflecting Samsung's order reduction 3 months ago. The model was last trained 14 months ago and treats Samsung's current lower order volume as an anomaly rather than a structural shift. Bias has worsened every cycle for 3 straight cycles (+0.12 → +0.17 → +0.23). A prior incident 14 months ago had the same driver — a retrain with refreshed ACV data improved wMAPE by 2.1 points within 2 cycles.

Model last trained 14 months ago — predates the Samsung order shift
Prior incident INC-028 (14 months ago, same driver): retrain with ACV refresh improved wMAPE 2.1 pts in 2 cycles
